on it and pass it around, and the debugger even lists its items when you expand it, quietly running the query to do so. Most of the time the source is a small in-memory list that doesn't change, so a second pass gives the same answer in microseconds and nothing looks wrong.

allocates memory for every element. For a large stream you read exactly once, such as the lines of a big file, staying lazy is the better choice. Materialize when you'll read the results more than once, or when you need them to stop changing.
